xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3762: Overdeck Anywhere: adopt t3code-style multi-machine environment federation

plan.title: Overdeck Anywhere: adopt t3code-style multi-machine environment federation
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

references.label: PAN-1166 WS auth PR #4317 (prerequisite for live-revocation)

narratives.Problem: Overdeck has one machine-wide root token and one root-derived session cookie. There is no per-device credential, no revocation, and no public environment identity, and many dashboard routes check only Origin while the server binds 0.0.0.0. So another device can only reach a machine by holding its root secret, and LAN peers can already call origin-only routes without any credential.
narratives.Proposal: Make each Overdeck server a self-describing environment (GET /api/environment built on the existing environment-identity.ts), add a global remote request gate that requires a credential for every non-local /api and /events request, and add one-time pairing: `pan pair` issues a 10-minute single-use odp_ credential delivered in a #pair= URL fragment, which the target server exchanges for a revocable odk_ device session stored in the PAN-2351-form credential registry (~/.overdeck/access-tokens.json). Devices never receive the root session. `pan devices` and DELETE /api/devices/:id revoke a device and close its WebSocket and SSE connections. The desktop catalog/switcher, endpoint discovery, SSH launch and aggregated views are split into PAN-4402, PAN-4403, PAN-4404 and PAN-4405.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No desktop connection catalog, environment switcher, Electron safeStorage or Settings Connections/Devices UI (PAN-4402).
- No in-renderer multi-environment transport refactor, query-key rekeying or store partitioning (PAN-4402).
- No endpoint discovery, Tailscale Serve setup or automatic trusted-origin advertisement (PAN-4403).
- No SSH launch, port forwarding or remote install (PAN-4404).
- No aggregated cross-environment views (PAN-4405).
- No token scopes enforcement, `pan token` verb, scoped-token Settings UI or WS/SSE heartbeats (PAN-2351).
- No re-implementation of WebSocket upgrade auth; reuse PR #4317's ws-auth.ts.
- No edits to src/lib/config-yaml/schema.ts and no file-size allowlist raises.
- No change to local-only behavior for loopback callers when require_token_mint is off.
- No migration or re-minting of environment-id.json; the identity file format is unchanged.
- No live ownership transfer, transcript replication or cross-machine state merge.
- No relay, account-service or multi-user shared-session work.
- The root internal token and overdeck_session cookie are never sent to or issued for a paired device.

autoDecisions.summary: Split the whole PRD into PAN-3762 plus sibling issues PAN-4402 (desktop catalog, switcher, version gating), PAN-4403 (endpoint advertisement), PAN-4404 (desktop SSH launch) and PAN-4405 (aggregated views); the machine-readable ownership fixture stays with PAN-3863 W1.
autoDecisions.rationale: The renderer federation refactor alone touches 171 files (399 relative fetch calls, 356 query keys, one global store); desktop, SSH and endpoint work are independently shippable, and the swarm contract prefers sibling issues over a mega-plan.

autoDecisions.summary: PAN-3762 keeps environment descriptor, pairing, device sessions, revocation and a new remote request gate, with a sizeJustification.
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator's 2026-09-28 decision, PAN-3863's ownership table and PAN-2609's PRD name PAN-3762 as owner of identity, pairing and device sessions; pairing without the gate or revocation would ship an unsafe credential.

autoDecisions.summary: Create src/lib/access-tokens.ts in PAN-2351 W1's exact form (plus optional kind) if PAN-2351 has not landed, instead of blocking on PAN-2351.
autoDecisions.rationale: Mirrors the operator-approved 'whichever lands first' rule for the shared identity contract and avoids two credential stores (FR-17).

autoDecisions.summary: Paired browsers get a new overdeck_device cookie; the session mint never issues the root-derived overdeck_session to a device credential.
autoDecisions.rationale: overdeck_session is an HMAC of the internal token, identical for every browser and not revocable; reusing it would make pairing grant permanent root access (FR-16).

autoDecisions.summary: Close validate-origin-only routes with one global HttpRouter middleware and an explicit unauthenticated allowlist, not per-route edits.
autoDecisions.rationale: Many routes only call validateOrigin and the server binds 0.0.0.0; one middleware covers every current and future route (FR-15).

autoDecisions.summary: Read dashboard.require_token_mint from raw config.yaml in src/lib/remote-access/config.ts rather than the config schema.
autoDecisions.rationale: src/lib/config-yaml/schema.ts is at its file-size cap and raising caps is an operator decision; readTraefikConfigFromYaml() is the existing precedent.

autoDecisions.summary: Pairing credentials live only in dashboard memory: single use, 10-minute TTL, 10 failures per 60 s rate limit.
autoDecisions.rationale: Short-lived secrets need no durable store; a restart invalidating them is safe and documented.

autoDecisions.summary: WebSocket revocation (live-revocation) waits for PR #4317 (PAN-1166) instead of re-implementing WebSocket auth.
autoDecisions.rationale: #4317 is complete and open; /ws/* upgrades bypass HttpRouter middleware, and duplicating its ws-auth.ts would create a second auth chokepoint.

autoDecisions.summary: Endpoint discovery and advertised trusted origins move to PAN-4403; until then operators set OVERDECK_TRUSTED_ORIGINS and pan pair takes --url.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps this slice focused on the security boundary; the docs state the manual step.

metadata.sizeJustification: Pairing, device-credential verification, the remote request gate and revocation that closes every live surface form one security boundary: shipping any subset leaves either an unrevocable credential, a device that can escalate to the root session, or network-reachable routes that trust no credential at all. Everything separable (desktop client, endpoints, SSH, aggregation) is already split into PAN-4402..4405. The 42-file count is mostly one new test file per item plus five doc files.
metadata.traceNote: FR-3, FR-5, FR-6, FR-10, FR-12, FR-13, NFR-8 and NFR-9 are owned by sibling issues PAN-4402, PAN-4404 and PAN-4405 per the PRD 'Decomposition (2026-09-29)' table.

narrative.Action: Implement W2.1 of the PRD .pan/drafts/pan-3762.md, section "This issue's implementation (2026-09-29)", following D-3762-2 and D-3762-3. If src/lib/access-tokens.ts already exists on origin/main (PAN-2351 landed), keep its API and add only the optional kind field and the cache functions. Otherwise create it exactly per PAN-2351 W1 (.pan/drafts/pan-2351.md): file ${OVERDECK_HOME}/access-tokens.json, mode 0600, atomic temp-file-then-rename writes, token odk_${randomBytes(32).toString('hex')}, SHA-256 hex at rest, timingSafeEqual compare, record {id, name, scopes, tokenHash, createdAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt?, kind?: 'device'|'token'}. API: createAccessToken({name, scopes, kind}) -> {token, record}; listAccessTokens() (no tokenHash); revokeAccessToken(id); verifyAccessToken(presented) synchronous against an in-memory snapshot; refreshAccessTokens() async; startAccessTokenRefresh()/stopAccessTokenRefresh() (unref'd 5 s async stat interval). lastUsedAt writes are async and throttled to once per record per minute. Corrupt/unreadable file = zero valid tokens and refreshAccessTokens rejects naming the path (fail closed). Import only Node built-ins and ./paths.js. Tests use vi.useFakeTimers() for cache refresh and throttling; never real waits.

Journey: issue a credential via POST /api/pairing/credentials with the internal token; open /#pair=<credential> in a fresh context; assert the dashboard loads, the overdeck_device cookie exists, no overdeck_session cookie exists and the URL has no #pair=; revoke through DELETE /api/devices/:id; assert the next /api/* call returns 401 and the RPC socket closes. Save and inspect screenshots of the loaded dashboard and of the post-revocation state.

items.title: Given a fresh isolated browser context, when it opens /#pair=<credential>, then the dashboard renders, the overdeck_device cookie is set, no overdeck_session cookie exists and the URL no longer contains #pair=
Given the paired context, when its device is revoked through DELETE /api/devices/:id, then its next /api/* request returns 401 and its /ws/rpc socket closes
Given the run, when it finishes, then it produces two screenshot files of the loaded and revoked states
